findings.evidence: "Also, the benefits team reviews the reimbursement log on the first business day of the month. The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Either describe what the review actually does (e.g., what happens to discrepancies found) or remove the "supersedes" sentence if no versioned document is being published.
findings.violation: "Reviews" doesn't produce "versions" that "supersede" one another - that sentence pattern only makes sense for a published document, not a review action, suggesting boilerplate was copied without adapting it to this context.

findings.evidence: "The stipend clock resumes on their first day back."
findings.fix: Replace "stipend clock" with the specific mechanism it refers to (e.g., "the 90-day eligibility waiting period").
findings.violation: "Stipend clock" is never defined - it's unclear whether this refers to the 90-day service requirement, the once-per-benefit-year claim window, or something else.

findings.evidence: "the stipend request, once the manager signs it, after finance confirms the budget line, moves to final processing"
findings.fix: Rewrite as a simple sequence, e.g., "After the manager signs the request and finance confirms the budget line, it moves to final processing."
findings.violation: The nested clauses make the order of operations ambiguous - it's unclear whether the manager signs before or after finance confirms the budget line.

findings.evidence: "Then, the employee reviews the confirmation summary before submitting the final request."
findings.fix: Move this step earlier in the section, before the manager/finance approval sentence, or clarify how it relates to the already-completed processing.
findings.violation: This step is placed after the confirmation email that supposedly ends processing, yet it describes reviewing a summary "before submitting the final request" - contradicting the sequence just given.

findings.evidence: "The manager reviews the request within two business days... The requester gets an automatic reminder after three days."
findings.fix: Use consistent units (e.g., "three business days") and clarify how the reminder threshold relates to the two-day review period.
findings.violation: The document mixes "business days" and plain "days" without clarifying whether the three-day reminder threshold uses the same unit as the two-day review window, making the timeline impossible to verify.

findings.evidence: "A photo of the receipt is enough for most requests."
findings.fix: List the specific criteria or request types that require more than a photo of the receipt.
findings.violation: "Most requests" is vague - it doesn't specify which requests require more than a photo or what the additional requirement would be.

findings.evidence: "You must keep your equipment in good working condition and we may ask for a brief photo check once a year."
findings.fix: Rewrite in the same third-person voice as the rest of the policy, e.g., "Employees must keep equipment in good working condition; the benefits team may request a brief photo check once a year."
findings.violation: This is the only place in the document written in second person ("you"/"we"), breaking from the third-person voice ("employees," "the finance office") used everywhere else.

findings.evidence: "we may ask for a brief photo check once a year"
findings.violation: "We" is undefined - the document otherwise names specific teams (benefits team, finance office, IT asset group), so it's unclear who conducts this check.

findings.evidence: "Similarly, the policy applies to one device per category per employee."
findings.fix: Replace "Similarly" with a neutral transition or move this sentence to the Eligibility section where claim limits are discussed.
findings.violation: "Similarly" implies a logical connection to the prior sentence about equipment condition and photo checks, but the one-device-per-category rule is unrelated.

findings.evidence: "You record the stipend item on the request form. Finance reconciles the reimbursable item against the request log each month. Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Pick one term for the purchased item and use it consistently throughout the document.
findings.violation: Three different terms ("stipend item," "reimbursable item," "covered purchase amount") are used for what appears to be the same thing without ever confirming they're synonymous, creating ambiguity about whether these are distinct concepts.

findings.evidence: "Payroll releases the covered purchase amount after that monthly review."
findings.fix: Reconcile the two sections so there is one stated payer and one stated timing rule for reimbursement.
findings.violation: This contradicts Reimbursement Amounts, which states "The finance office deposits the amount within one pay cycle" - two different actors (payroll vs. finance office) and two different timing rules (monthly review vs. one pay cycle) for the same payout.

findings.evidence: "Also, you submit the request in the portal. Countersign the employee request within two business days."
findings.fix: Name the actors explicitly instead of using "you" (e.g., "The employee submits the request; the manager countersigns it within two business days").
findings.violation: The pronoun "you" appears to refer to the same person for both submitting and countersigning the request, which would mean the employee approves their own request; this role is presumably the manager's, per Approval Timeline.

findings.evidence: "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility, and the uploaded receipt."
findings.fix: Rewrite as a complete list of steps, e.g., "Completing the request begins with confirming eligibility and uploading a receipt."
findings.violation: The sentence is grammatically malformed - "the uploaded receipt" is not a parallel action to "confirming eligibility," leaving the step list incomplete or fragmentary.

findings.evidence: "The IT asset group updates the equipment catalog after every open enrollment period."
findings.fix: Reconcile ownership and cadence of the equipment catalog into a single consistent statement.
findings.violation: This contradicts Program Overview, which states "The benefits team publishes the equipment catalog on the first business day of the month" - two different owners and two different update schedules for the same catalog.

findings.evidence: "A separate audit last spring reviewed unrelated travel expenses. Federal guidance on remote work continues to evolve each year. The office coffee budget was reset at the start of the quarter."
findings.fix: Remove the unrelated sentences or move any relevant content to an appropriate section with an explanation of its relevance.
findings.violation: These sentences are explicitly unrelated to the stipend policy (travel expenses, federal guidance, coffee budget) and add no actionable information, cluttering the policy document.

findings.evidence: "The finance office reviews every stipend request over 200 dollars before it pays out."
findings.fix: Integrate this threshold into the Approval Timeline section so the full approval sequence is described in one place.
findings.violation: This introduces a new approval gate (a $200 threshold triggering finance review) that is never mentioned in the Approval Timeline section, leaving the overall approval process fragmented and incomplete.

findings.evidence: "The finance office also flags any request that repeats within the same quarter."
findings.fix: Clarify whether this refers to resubmitted/corrected requests versus new claims, and reconcile with the one-claim-per-year rule.
findings.violation: This conflicts with Eligibility's statement that the stipend "covers one claim per employee per benefit year" - it's unclear how a request could legitimately repeat within the same quarter under that limit.

findings.evidence: "The finance liaison publishes the vendor list on the first business day of the month. The most recent version supersedes the one that came before it."
findings.fix: Explain what the vendor list is used for in this policy, or remove the reference if it's out of scope.
findings.violation: "Vendor list" is mentioned nowhere else in the document, so its purpose and relevance to the stipend program are undefined; the sentence also duplicates boilerplate used verbatim in Program Overview for a different document (the reimbursement log).
